new_findings.title: D6's premise 'free cells are observed space' is false under D4: the hand is in the eye's frame at home, the robot never casts a shadow, and D8's table-plane footprint does not bound 3-D free cells
new_findings.problem: D6 never casts an interior at a place destination 'because the robot places only into free cells, and free cells are observed space (D8 window restricts free space to the eye's view)'. Free space is not a record of observation: it is the workspace box minus the registered OBJECT and SHADOW AABBs (free_space.py:47-48, 86-102; reboxelize.py:41-46). Shadows are cast only from registered task bodies (boxel_env.py:1506-1513); the detector drops 'robot' from its body map (boxel_env.py:1749-1752) and register_new_detections skips it (execution.py:2296). D4 itself says that at home 'its hand is in frame exactly as in their check' (:329-330), so the table region the hand hides from the eye at t=0 is neither SHADOW nor OBJECT: it becomes free space, enters the placement candidates, and _build_init emits obj_at_boxel_KIF(target, cell) for it (pddlstream_planner.py:679-681) on audit #67's premise 'the fixed overhead camera covers the entire table' (pddlstream_planner.py:667-670), which is false for the D4 eye. A cup partly behind the hand at t=0 is likewise unregistered and its volume becomes free. Second, D8 intersects the window with the TABLE-PLANE frustum footprint, while free cells reach table + 0.5 m (free_space.py:48); near the far frustum edges the column above a footprint point leaves the frustum, so a cup's cavity placed there covers volume the eye never imaged. The 'observational justification' D6 adds over methods.tex:157 holds only under these unstated assumptions, and the paper would state it as fact.
new_findings.evidence: plan_v2.txt:329-331, 366-375, 411-415; free_space.py:47-48, 86-102; reboxelize.py:41-46; boxel_env.py:1506-1513, 1749-1752; execution.py:2296; pddlstream_planner.py:667-681
new_findings.required_change: (a) B1(e) adds a measurement: render the table with task bodies parked (throwaway client) from the D4 eye with the arm at DEFAULT_ARM_POS, back-project the robot's seg pixels onto the table plane and through the slab up to the largest declared cavity height, and record that robot-occluded footprint in BF#2. (b) D8 subtracts it from the window (a constant derived once from the URDF and the eye pose, G9-allowed) and applies the frustum test to each free cell's 3-D corners up to that slab height, not to the table-plane footprint alone. (c) Reword D6: 'free cells are the complement of the registered OBJECT and SHADOW regions inside a window W that the t=0 render images unoccluded (BF#2), which under the 2.5-D shadow model is observed space'. (d) File a BF# restating audit #67's premise for the D4 eye (observed_clear_regions=None is valid only inside W), since every free-cell Know-If in the init rests on it.

new_findings.title: M2 inherits the rediscovery cleanup that deletes a caster's fragments from the belief without a render, and D6's rediscovery clause casts an interior at a place destination
new_findings.problem: D6 casts an interior 'when a hollow body is REGISTERED from a render (initial boxelization, discovery, rediscovery)' and wires it 'exactly like a lateral fragment'. The sense discovery path re-registers an already registered body by first deleting every id in old_obj.shadow_boxel_ids from the registry AND the belief (execution.py:2871-2884, belief.remove_shadow) with no render of those grids, then casting fresh fragments at the body's CURRENT pose (execution.py:2973-3003). If the interior id is listed in the cup's shadow_boxel_ids (it must be for retire_lost_objects to test it, execution.py:2110-2118), a relocated cup that a later sense hits inside some fragment loses its ORIGINAL interior region unobserved (possibly the die's region), and gets a NEW interior at its current pose, which is a place destination, where D6 says an interior is 'NEVER cast'. G5 ledgers only ids passed as known_empty, so neither the deletion nor the re-cast is caught, and B5's abort clause names only 'marks an interior region not_here', not removal.
new_findings.evidence: plan_v2.txt:366-375, 569-583, 95-100; execution.py:2862-2884 (cleanup with belief.remove_shadow), 2973-3003 (re-cast at current pose), 2105-2125 (retire_lost_objects tests by render)
new_findings.required_change: B5 specification: (1) interior ids are exempt from the rediscovery cleanup at execution.py:2871-2884 (a separate interior_boxel_ids list), or the cleanup keeps every fragment that does not pass _fragment_renders_empty, as retire_lost_objects does; (2) pre-register the rediscovery precedence now: a hollow body casts an interior on its first registration and on re-registration after it was lost, never on a rediscovery at a ledgered place destination (or the opposite, disclosed), but decided before B5; (3) extend G5 so every id that leaves the belief (remove_shadow, mark_sensed found=False, mark_unresolved) carries a provenance row, and a removal without a render of that grid fails the gate; B5's abort clause reads 'removes from the belief or marks not_here without a render of its grid'.

new_findings.title: M1 is the archived at_sense_config gate turned into a planned move: its POD justification is false at q_clear, B1(h) never tests q_clear, and the shared q_home symbol couples the sense gate to D7's 1e-4 scoring test
new_findings.problem: (a) M1 says Pre(Y) 'now states that the robot's own body is clear of the fixed eye', but D4 says the hand is in the eye's frame at home (:329-330): at q_clear the robot is not clear of the eye. B1(h) measures blocking only at post-place lift poses and only for interior regions; it never measures the blocked fraction of any region (interior or lateral) at q_clear, the pose M1 makes the sufficient condition. A region the hand hides at home goes still_blocked three times, is parked and is handed to the planner as not_here (execution.py:3061-3079; test_full_pipeline.py:1217-1218). (b) 'one object, two roles': D7 gives the 1e-4 final hold to 'a move whose target is a declared goal configuration' and the home_not_reached bound to 'moves to q_home', so under M1 every pre-sense move gets the hold and counts toward the bound, and the plan does not say whether at_config(q_clear) for sense is the move's symbolic effect (today current_config takes q2.name whatever the residual, test_full_pipeline.py:1591-1597) or D7's 1e-4 evaluator. That coupling is the archived design: archive/tampura_bridge_v1/sense_config.py:28-41 allowed sensing only at DEFAULT_ARM_POS through is_at_sense_config(atol=1e-4), documented as 'the at-home gate reused', and boxel_policy.py:54 put (at_sense_config) in the init. The record does not cite this lineage. (c) M1 AFTER writes (at_config q_clear) as a constant, while B4 emits (sense_config q_clear), a predicate absent from pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl:20-80, which implies a new sense parameter and a new static predicate that BEFORE/AFTER does not declare and G10 cannot check against a declared delta. (d) The CLAIM EFFECT keeps methods.tex:170, but :170 also says 'the only geometric precondition is the derived predicate (view_clear ?region)', and the sense listing methods.tex:141-148 already omits handempty and boxel_fits (domain_pddlstream.pddl:174, 183); under M1 it would be three preconditions stale.
new_findings.required_change: (1) Reword the M1 justification: 'at q_clear the robot occludes exactly what it occluded in the t=0 render from which the regions were cast'. (2) B1(h) also renders every region kind (interior and lateral, all three layouts) with the arm at q_clear and records the worst blocked fraction; above 0.05 for any region, M1 is not sufficient and the record says so before B7. (3) Decide now: at_config(q_clear) as a sense precondition is the executed move's symbolic effect (B1(h) also shows the clearance holds at the 2e-3 rad settle residual), and the 1e-4 evaluator, the final hold and home_not_reached apply only to the goal conjunct (the move home while holding the target); or q_clear is a distinct symbol. (4) M1 BEFORE/AFTER states the exact PDDL delta (constant, or new parameter plus static predicate) that G10 regenerates. (5) The M1 BF# cites the archived at_sense_config and states the differences (planned move, geometry-decided, no teleport, no shared tolerance). (6) The claim effect lists methods.tex:141-148 and the 'only geometric precondition' sentence of :170, and P4.5 CORRECTIONS adds the stale sense listing (handempty, boxel_fits).

new_findings.title: M2's partition statement leaves K(not InBoxel(target, hollow OBJECT boxel)) false in the true world and does not state how interiors are carved against existing fragments
new_findings.problem: _build_init emits obj_at_boxel_KIF(target, b) for every OBJECT boxel, justified in code as 'only emit known not here if this region has been observed clear' (pddlstream_planner.py:667-673). Under M2 the cup's OBJECT box contains its cavity and the die lies inside that volume, so under the thesis's geometric reading of InBoxel (methods.tex:84 'which Boxel a hidden object occupies', :97) the initial belief asserts a known-not-here literal that is false, about a region never observed clear. The partition statement admits the shared volume but does not redefine InBoxel for a hollow OBJECT boxel. Separately, audit #68 is enforced by carving each new fragment against all existing SHADOW boxels (boxel_env.py:1510-1511; execution.py:2352-2357); the interior of a hollow body registered mid-episode inside a still-unknown lateral fragment either overlaps it (invariant false) or is carved away (the cavity then belongs to the other fragment). 'Still holds' needs the rule.
new_findings.required_change: Partition statement: 'for a hollow class the OBJECT boxel denotes the shell (the box minus its interior region) for InBoxel; K(not InBoxel(target, shell)) rests on the observed outer surface and the solid walls'. B5: the interior is carved against existing SHADOW fragments and against OBJECT boxels other than its own caster's, as lateral fragments are, and the paper's sentence on audit #68 says so.

new_findings.title: Correction 1 calls accurate thesis wording wrong and misses the sentence that is actually inaccurate
new_findings.problem: methods.tex:168 already says the blocked shadow 'is marked empty without ever being directly observed ... it is unsound', and results.tex:464-469 says the loop 'marks it as not containing the target', that it is never observed, and that the run report distinguishes the two; both match the code (planner literal not_here, BeliefState unresolved). Correction 1 declares this wording wrong. The inaccurate sentence is results.tex:469-470 'the evaluation counts the give-up case as a failure': only an episode that ends all_searched without the target fails (test_full_pipeline.py:1260-1271), and a give-up followed by finding the target elsewhere is a success. Also methods.tex:168 says re-grounding the view-blocking facts 'is left to future work', while test_full_pipeline.py:1053-1055 says the re-ground 'landed with #P1 F2's blocks_view_at re-keying'.
new_findings.required_change: Rewrite correction 1: keep methods.tex:168 and results.tex:464-468 (accurate); correct results.tex:469-470 to 'an episode that ends with only given-up regions left and no target is a failure'; reconcile methods.tex:168's future-work sentence with the F2 re-keying. The audit record must not state the thesis is wrong where it is right.

new_findings.title: P4.8 presents the planned sense as the only observation channel; the pipeline also observes passively at every render
new_findings.problem: P4.8 says Y_R is obtained under Pre(Y_R) = view_clear(R) and handempty (and at_config(q_clear) under M1). The pipeline also writes Y_R outside the planned sense: sweep_all_fragments removes any fragment whose grid renders clear_but_empty in the sense render (execution.py:2185-2201), retire_lost_objects marks a lost caster's fragments not_here from integrity renders taken with the arm anywhere (execution.py:2110-2118; test_full_pipeline.py:1740-1743), and register_new_detections registers a visible target at any render (execution.py:2255-2285), which B5 and G15 accept as discovery. Under M1 these happen while at_config(q_clear) is false. All are render-gated and sound, but the LW1 statement misdescribes when observations arrive.
new_findings.required_change: P4.8 adds: 'a second, passive channel: every render evaluates every region's grid and every visible body with the render's own visibility test as its precondition, not a planner literal; it writes found, not_here (all endpoints seen) or a new occluder, never a parked status; in LW1 terms these are observables whose preconditions are not modelled in the domain and are absorbed by replanning'. G5's provenance enumerates these channels by name.
